expert_diagnosis: Jet Airways collapsed from a combination of unsustainable debt, high fixed operating costs incompatible with a low-cost-dominated market, failed emergency funding rescue, and the irreversible value destruction from operational suspension. The lender committee's refusal to provide emergency funds removed the last lifeline. Root causes: cash liquidity crisis, debt solvency pressure, failed emergency funding and rescue, high operating-cost structure, competitive pressure from LCCs, loss of operating continuity from suspension, creditor coordination complexity, and cross-border insolvency complexity.
expert_first_action: Immediate lender standstill and IBC-protected restructuring to halt value destruction; preserve aircraft slots, routes, and key assets; develop a funded revival plan anchored on a viable reduced network; stabilize employee, customer, and creditor obligations; coordinate Indian and cross-border (Dutch) stakeholders simultaneously.
actual_decision: No emergency rescue funding was secured. Operations remained suspended. NCLT insolvency petition was admitted 20 June 2019.
harmful_actions: Failure to secure emergency rescue funding before operational suspension
Delay in seeking formal insolvency protection while value (slots, routes, assets) eroded
Failure to resolve cross-border coordination before operational collapse
beneficial_actions: Lender committee's eventual decision to pursue formal IBC process preserved some structured value-recovery pathway
citation: NCLT Mumbai admitted petition 20 June 2019, appointed Interim Resolution Professional. Supreme Court of India directed liquidation November 2024 after multi-year revival effort. Dutch bankruptcy proceedings from May 2019. Jet Airways official insolvency page and IBBI order confirm CIRP commencement.
actual_outcome: NCLT Mumbai admitted insolvency petition 20 June 2019 and appointed Interim Resolution Professional. Dutch bankruptcy proceedings ran from May 2019. Multi-year revival effort under Jalan-Kalrock consortium ultimately failed. Supreme Court directed liquidation in November 2024.
documented_root_causes: Cash liquidity crisis — insufficient to continue operations
Debt solvency pressure — heavily debt-laden balance sheet
Failed emergency funding rescue — lenders declined April 2019
High operating-cost structure — uncompetitive with LCCs
Loss of operating continuity from suspension — slots and routes at risk
Creditor coordination complexity across multiple creditor classes
final_business_state: CIRP commenced June 2019. Multi-year revival attempt failed. Supreme Court directed liquidation November 2024.
